rules.title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or its agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The limit is adjusted each year by the Director of the Division of Consumer Affairs in proportion to the percent change in the Consumer Price Index, but only when that change is greater than zero.
rules.key_value: $50, adjusted annually in direct proportion to the percent change in the Consumer Price Index (only if the change is greater than zero)
rules.coverage_text: Landlords and their agents charging application or similar fees to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes.
rules.exemptions: A dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent. A licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission, unless the licensee is the landlord of the property.
rules.penalty: Penalty of up to $500 for a first offense, up to $750 for a second offense, and up to $1,000 for each subsequent offense, enforced by summary proceedings under the Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999. The amount wrongfully charged is taken from the collected penalty and remitted to the applicant or prospective tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply

This act shall take effect on the first day of the
